WITH baseline_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(modindex) AS baseline_avg
  FROM signals
  WHERE modindex IS NOT NULL
),
group_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(rfistat, 'no status') AS status,
    AVG(modindex) AS avg_modindex
  FROM signals
  WHERE modindex IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY COALESCE(rfistat, 'no status')
),
with_baseline_comparison AS (
  SELECT 
    ga.status,
    ga.avg_modindex,
    bc.baseline_avg
  FROM group_averages ga
  CROSS JOIN baseline_calc bc
  WHERE ga.avg_modindex > bc.baseline_avg
),
mean_of_kept_averages AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_modindex) AS mean_kept
  FROM with_baseline_comparison
)
SELECT 
  wbc.status,
  wbc.avg_modindex AS average_modulation_index,
  wbc.avg_modindex - wbc.baseline_avg AS above_baseline,
  wbc.avg_modindex - mka.mean_kept AS differs_from_mean_of_kept
FROM with_baseline_comparison wbc
CROSS JOIN mean_of_kept_averages mka
ORDER BY wbc.status;

assumptions.assumption: Signals with NULL rfistat are grouped as a single 'no status' category, treated identically to named RFI statuses for selection and metrics
The baseline average includes all signals with non-NULL modindex values regardless of their RFI status
A status qualifies as 'above baseline' using strict inequality (> not >=)
